clue.text: Without reversing, large car arrived in plant

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for arrived goes round the other piece

parts.note: arrived means came

indicators.note: reversing tells us the word for a large car is written back to front

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a large car

explanation.surface: Someone parks a limousine among the plants without backing it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'not', but here it is the old sense 'outside', a containment signal; 'reversing' turns only the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile is a daisy-like herb, a flowering species used for tea.

clue.text: 'oly — that's admitted

definitions.meaning: 'oly is holy with the h dropped Cockney style, so the word for sacred used of a name or ground loses its h in the same way
admitted means let in or permitted

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'oly shows a dropped h; the matching word for holy, said by a Cockney, also loses its h and becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred, said with a dropped h, sounds like the answer, and being let in means being permitted.

clue.text: One of 22 — supervisor has it

definitions.meaning: 22 across is the entry for mistakes, and one such is a slip or lapse
a supervisor has charge or supervision of work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a careless omission, one item in a list of mistakes, and the watchful management a supervisor exercises.

clue.text: Drop in this month — I travel at the end

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of travel

explanation.surface: A traveller plans to drop in on someone late this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is old commercial shorthand for 'this month'; 'at the end' takes L, the last letter of 'travel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to introduce a liquid gradually, drop by drop, so to put drops in.

clue.text: In France, the men's struggle for Liberation

indicators.note: struggle suggests the letters wrestle themselves into a new order

explanation.surface: French men fight for their country's freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' rearranges all of IN FRANCE THE MEN'S, including the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting freedom, as to slaves, or granting the vote is a form of liberation.

clue.text: Aboard a warship by choice

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so one piece is carried inside the vessel's word

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a warship
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone serves on a naval vessel voluntarily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by choice' looks like one phrase meaning voluntarily, but 'by' is wordplay and 'choice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means of top quality, excellent.

clue.text: Airs from cobbler disheartened Mr Pleydell

parts.note: snob is an old word for a cobbler or shoemaker

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letter of the name

parts.note: Berry Pleydell is the hero of Dornford Yates's Berry and Co stories

explanation.surface: A shoemaker's pretensions dispirit a gentleman customer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dornford Yates's interwar comic novels follow Berry Pleydell; his name loses its central R. SNOB as cobbler is an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means acting superior, the hallmark of social pretension.

clue.text: Charm dispelled — a rum one

indicators.note: dispelled suggests the letters are scattered and then reassembled

explanation.surface: A spell is broken by a strange character.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to captivate, to fill with love.

clue.text: Rebel taking a rest elsewhere

parts.note: a break is a rest
away means somewhere else

explanation.surface: An insurgent takes a holiday somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group that rebels and splits from a larger body is described this way.

clue.text: Plowman accepts money for a tool

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the name holds the money letter inside it

parts.note: Piers Plowman is the medieval poem by Langland, so Plowman suggests Piers
L, for pound (Latin libra), stands for money

explanation.surface: A farmer takes payment in exchange for an implement.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Plowman is William Langland's 14th-century poem; its hero's first name takes in L (pound, money).
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a gripping hand implement with pivoted jaws.

clue.text: Agent for developing part of building

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters are being worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: An estate agent is busy developing a section of a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges AGENT FOR; 'for' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontage is the face of a building looking onto a street.

clue.text: Cross about a set of tools having several cutters

indicators.note: about indicates turning round, here applied to the whole run of pieces read back together

parts.note: a kit is a set of tools
saws are cutters, several of them making a plural

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed with a toolkit full of saws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the whole run A KIT SAWS; 'Cross' looks like the adjective meaning angry but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The swastika is a hooked cross, an ancient symbol later used by the Nazis.

clue.text: Made oneself go to vet after tiny creature lost its tail

indicators.note: after says the words to vet come after the creature in the answer
lost its tail means the final letter of the creature's name is dropped

parts.note: a bee is a tiny creature
to vet is to check and pass, to OK

explanation.surface: Someone dragged themselves to the vet after their little pet lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used with 'oneself' (he betook himself home), which is why the definition includes 'oneself'. 'lost its tail' cuts BEE to BE.
explanation.definitionFit: To betake oneself is an old idiom meaning to go somewhere, so the past form means made oneself go.

clue.text: Saw a girl, for instance, on the way back

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: on the way back means the abbreviation is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation meaning for instance

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a young woman, for example, while returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see but is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb.

clue.text: A story portraying degradation

parts.note: a basement is a storey of a building, here spelt story

explanation.surface: A tale depicting someone's humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' is a floor of a building (storey); the lowest one gives BASEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation, a lowering in dignity.

clue.text: Untidy person causing trouble in county retreat

indicators.note: in tells us the word for trouble sits inside the other piece
retreat means go backwards, so the county's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county
care, as in worry or bother, means trouble

explanation.surface: A scruffy individual stirs up a fuss at a country hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns the county abbreviation round, and 'in' places the trouble just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a person in ragged, shabby clothes is likened to the straw figure set up in a field.

clue.text: Companion in first part of trip omitted from book's opening

indicators.note: omitted from means the letter is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: chapter one is the opening of a book

indicators.note: first part of picks the opening letter of trip

explanation.surface: A travel companion appears early in the story of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part of' gives T, from 'trip', and 'omitted from' takes it out of CHAPTER ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is an older companion who escorts a young person.

clue.text: Royalist's ace rival beaten

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A king's supporter defeats his top opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royalist's' is Royalist is; the 's links definition to wordplay. 'beaten' rearranges ACE RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers were supporters of Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: A country opened up by trailbreaking

definitions.text: A country opened up by trailbreaking

indicators.note: opened up by means the first pieces are split apart and the other letters go inside

parts.note: the USA is a country

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of trail are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A nation whose interior was first made accessible by pioneers blazing new routes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a country whose interior was explored by trailblazers.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a nation whose vast interior was opened up by pioneering explorers.

clue.text: Paid about a sovereign for antique instrument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the payment word goes round the monarch's letters

parts.note: spent means paid out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a sovereign

explanation.surface: Someone paid around a gold coin for an old musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the gold coin but means a monarch, given by the Queen's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent is an obsolete bass wind instrument shaped in snaking curves.

clue.text: Politicians do

definitions.meaning: politicians as one collective body, those of one parliamentary group
a do is informal British for a celebration or social event

explanation.definitionFit: A political grouping is a body of politicians, and a do is a social gathering or celebration.

clue.text: In the Jobcentre, a clerk offers blandishments

indicators.note: In says the answer lies inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A benefits office worker sweet-talks claimants.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a UK government job and benefits office.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle figuratively means cloying flattery or sentimentality.

clue.text: Things dropped from planes over the States

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the planes above the piece for the States

parts.note: jets are planes
Am., short for America, stands for the States

explanation.surface: Objects fall from aircraft flying over America.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard, goods cast off from a ship.

clue.text: In time deserter makes mistakes

indicators.note: In at the start tells us the deserter's word is placed inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A soldier who abandoned his post in due course gets things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: These are errors, especially those listed for correction in a printed book.

clue.text: Miser using wood, we hear, and almost nothing beside

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for the wood is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: ebony is a dense black wood

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted man makes do with timber and next to nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: EBONY said aloud gives the start of the name, EBENE; ZERO without its last letter ('almost') gives ZER; 'beside' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, is the archetypal skinflint.

clue.text: Flower cries out for use

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river: the Exe in Devon

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of cries are disordered

explanation.surface: A bloom shouts out to be put to some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river (it flows): the Exe, a river in Devon. 'out' rearranges CRIES to CISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to employ it.

clue.text: Char to copy Jehu

definitions.meaning: to char is to burn the surface of something
Jehu, the biblical king known for furious chariot driving, is a byword for a fast driver, so to copy him is to drive very fast

explanation.definitionFit: Singeing burns a surface, and the same word was once slang for racing along a road at reckless speed, like Jehu's furious driving.

clue.text: Aquatic creature on right side of first rock

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, the creature following the letter
right side of means the final letter, the one at the right-hand end of the word

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: An otter is perched on the right-hand side of the first rock.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to sway unsteadily, much as something rocks back and forth.

clue.text: Chap about to enter part of garden covered with trees

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, so a chap

indicators.note: to enter means the word for about goes inside the garden piece

parts.note: a bed is a part of a garden for plants
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man is about to step into a leafy bit of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbered land is wooded, standing timber being trees grown for wood.
